body.statement: The promise problem \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\) is \(\forall\mathbb R\)-complete. For every \(Q\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{sel}}\), \(\mathsf C\) outputs in polynomial time an acyclic mixed graph \(G_Q\) of maximum directed indegree at most two, a rational strictly diagonally dominant matrix \(\Sigma_Q\), the selector-master edge \(e_Q\), and the rational feasible matrix \(\rho_Q\). The master projection \(\pi_Q\) is a bijection \(\mathcal F_{G_Q}(\Sigma_Q)\to\operatorname{Sol}(Q)\), with occurrence replication as its inverse, and \(L_{e_Q}=(\pi_Q(L))_{s_Q}\) for every \(L\in\mathcal F_{G_Q}(\Sigma_Q)\). Consequently, \(Q\in\mathsf{coSEL\mbox{-}PNQF}\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal A_{e_Q}(G_Q,\Sigma_Q)=\{0\}\Longleftrightarrow\mathsf C(Q)\in\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\), whereas \(Q\in\mathsf{SEL\mbox{-}PNQF}\Longleftrightarrow\mathcal A_{e_Q}(G_Q,\Sigma_Q)=\{0,1\}\). Thus \(\mathsf C\) is a promise-preserving many-one reduction from the complemented language, not from the uncomplemented language. Relative to Dörfler et al., the strict tightening is maximum directed indegree two together with a fiber-bijective compiler.
body.justification: The exact promise polarity and fiber bijection certify that fan-in two already carries the full universal real-algebraic obstruction.
body.gap: Dörfler et al., Corollary 4 and Theorem 14, establish unrestricted promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-completeness, but their Section 4 storage sink has fan-in growing with the source instance; the strict delta is a maximum-directed-indegree-two, fiber-bijective compilation.
body.consumer: Algorithm designers for SEM identification obtain a precise reason not to expect a complete polynomial-time extension of the fan-in-one audit to two-parent equations.
body.proof_tex:
We first verify the compiler at the level of its entire fiber.  Use a depth-one directed graph in which every coefficient-holding sink \(i\) has a private parent set \(P_i\) of size at most two, every parent is a root used by only that sink, and all programmed equations are assigned to distinct missing pairs of sinks.  If \(i\) and \(j\) are such a pair, then direct expansion gives
\[
\Omega(L)_{ij}
=\Sigma_{ij}
-\sum_{a\in P_i}\Sigma_{aj}L_{ai}
-\sum_{b\in P_j}\Sigma_{ib}L_{bj}
+\sum_{a\in P_i}\sum_{b\in P_j}\Sigma_{ab}L_{ai}L_{bj}.
\]
Thus any prescribed bi-affine equation
\[
c+u^{\mathsf T}x+v^{\mathsf T}y+x^{\mathsf T}Wy=0
\]
is obtained by setting \(\Sigma_{ij}=c\), \(\Sigma_{aj}=-u_a\), \(\Sigma_{ib}=-v_b\), and \(\Sigma_{ab}=W_{ab}\).  Because every root is private, each slot \(\Sigma_{aj}\), \(\Sigma_{ib}\), or \(\Sigma_{ab}\) identifies the same unordered pair of owner sinks \(\{i,j\}\); hence it cannot be used by a different programmed equation.  The constant slot \(\Sigma_{ij}\) is likewise pair-specific.

For each source coordinate make a singleton master coefficient.  For every occurrence in a constraint make a fresh coefficient.  An addition \(a+b=c\) uses a two-coefficient sink carrying \((a,b)\) and a singleton sink carrying \(c\); a multiplication \(ab=c\) uses a two-coefficient sink carrying \((a,c)\) and a singleton carrying \(b\).  Equality and constant constraints use singleton occurrence sinks, paired when necessary with a fresh zero-parent sink.  The preceding covariance assignment realizes the desired residual in each case.

For an occurrence \(q\) of master \(v\), introduce a fresh singleton hub coefficient \(h_q\) and two distinct missing sink pairs realizing
\[
q-h_q=0,qquad h_q-v=0.
\]
Freshness ensures that these pairs remain distinct even for a repeated input.  Every occurrence and hub is therefore forced to equal exactly one master, and no coefficient introduced by copying is free.  Declare every other unordered vertex pair bidirected.  It follows that the missing-edge system consists of exactly the gate, constant, and copy equations just listed.

Let the programmed off-diagonal matrix be \(S\), and put
\[
H=1+\max_i\sum_{j\ne i}|S_{ij}|,
\qquad (\Sigma_Q)_{ii}=H.
\]
All quantities are rational and have polynomial bit length.  For every nonzero vector \(u\),
\[
u^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_Q u
\ge \sum_i\left(H-\sum_{j\ne i}|S_{ij}|\right)u_i^2
\ge \sum_i u_i^2>0,
\]
where \(2|u_i u_j|\le u_i^2+u_j^2\) was used in the first inequality.  Hence \(\Sigma_Q\) is strictly diagonally dominant and positive definite.  No programmed equation uses a diagonal slot, because roots and sinks are disjoint and every equation pair consists of distinct sinks (or a sink and a fresh zero-parent vertex).

Given \(x\in\operatorname{Sol}(Q)\), assign each master its coordinate and replicate that value to every occurrence and hub.  Every programmed equation then vanishes, producing a supported matrix \(R_Q(x)\in\mathcal F_{G_Q}(\Sigma_Q)\).  Conversely, the two copy equations force any \(L\) in the fiber to equal \(R_Q(\pi_Q(L))\), and the gate equations force \(\pi_Q(L)\in\operatorname{Sol}(Q)\).  Therefore
\[
\pi_Q\circ R_Q=\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Sol}(Q)},
\qquad
R_Q\circ\pi_Q=\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal F_{G_Q}(\Sigma_Q)}.
\]
This proves the fiber bijection.  Applying it to the rational planted vector gives the rational feasible coefficient matrix \(\rho_Q=R_Q(z_Q)\).  The graph is acyclic of depth one and each sink has at most two private parents.  The number of vertices and assigned covariance slots is linear in the number of masters, occurrences, hubs, and gates, so construction time and output bit length are polynomial.

The queried edge is the selector master.  Hence, for every fiber point,
\[
L_{e_Q}=(\pi_Q(L))_{s_Q}.
\]
The source promise supplies a selector-zero planted solution and restricts every solution to selector zero or one.  The bijection therefore gives
\[
\mathcal A_{e_Q}(G_Q,\Sigma_Q)
=\begin{cases}
\{0\},&Q\in\mathsf{coSEL\mbox{-}PNQF},\\
\{0,1\},&Q\in\mathsf{SEL\mbox{-}PNQF}.
\end{cases}
\]
Thus the compiler maps the complemented language, and not the uncomplemented language, to YES instances of \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\).  The source-language lemma proves promise \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness.

For membership, on a promised instance identification is the universal real sentence
\[
\forall L,L'\;\Bigl(
L,L'\text{ obey the support and all missing-edge equations}
\Longrightarrow L_e=L'_e
\Bigr).
\]
Support gives linear equations and every missing-edge residual has degree at most two with rational coefficients, so this is a polynomial-size universal formula over the reals.  Hence \(\mathsf{NUMEDGE}_2\) belongs to promise \(\forall\mathbb R\), proving completeness.  The cited published comparison records unrestricted \(\forall\mathbb R\)-hardness for numerical edge identifiability; the depth-one, indegree-two, fiber-bijective construction above proves the stated strict structural tightening.
